solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Plant initially cultivated using compost and brown earth (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: the start of each of the next three words is taken

blocks.note: first letters of cultivated, using, compost
umber is a brown earth used as a pigment

annotation.surface: A gardener's recipe for bringing on a plant: compost worked into good brown soil.
annotation.walkthrough: The gardening surface hides that 'initially' reaches across three words, not one, and that the brown earth is the painter's pigment rather than soil.
annotation.definitionFit: The cucumber is a trailing plant of the gourd family, grown for its fruit.

entries.clue: Young animal on a Caribbean island (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second

blocks.note: a cub is the young of a bear, lion or fox
used as printed

annotation.surface: A young animal sits on a Caribbean island.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed above: the cub sits on top of the A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cuba is one of many Caribbean islands, and the largest.

entries.clue: Manage Crown’s turmoil on a regular basis (7)

indicatorNotes.on a regular basis: take letters at regular intervals: every other one

blocks.note: C r O w N s T u R m O i L: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

annotation.surface: Someone must keep a lid on recurring trouble within the monarchy.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: the letters of CROWNS and TURMOIL run together as one string before every other letter is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: running or directing something, as in 'she controls the budget'.

entries.clue: Amoral pimp’s squirming and misspeaking (11)

annotation.definitionNote: 'misspeaking' is a gerund used as a noun, standing for the noun MALAPROPISM

indicatorNotes.squirming: letters that squirm twist about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, the S of the possessive included

annotation.surface: A crooked pimp writhes in discomfort and trips over his words.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive S is part of the fodder, which is easy to miss. A malapropism is the comic misuse of a similar-sounding word, named after Mrs Malaprop in Sheridan's play.
annotation.definitionFit: A malapropism is a verbal slip in which the wrong word is used, which is a kind of misspeaking.

entries.clue: Value fairness (6)

blocks.note: the value of a property or share once debts are taken away
the quality of being even-handed

annotation.surface: A two-word motto: prize fairness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Value' as a verb, but here it is a noun: the financial sense of equity, as in home equity.
annotation.definitionFit: Equity means both the net value of an asset and fairness or impartiality.

entries.clue: Computers brought round for fraudulent scheme (4)

indicatorNotes.brought round: turned round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Macs are Apple computers

annotation.surface: Computers are being ferried about as part of some crooked racket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brought round' sounds like delivery, but it tells you to turn the computers back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people.

entries.clue: Company restricting communist beliefs (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'beliefs' is plural; a credo is a single statement of beliefs

indicatorNotes.restricting: the company hems in the communist, holding it inside

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
red is the colour of communism

annotation.surface: A firm clamps down on the political convictions of a left-wing employee.
annotation.walkthrough: RED for a communist is a crossword regular, from the red flag.
annotation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs, from the Latin 'I believe'.

entries.clue: Government department is finally stopping car tax (8)

indicatorNotes.stopping: the S plugs the gap between the car and the tax, stopping them up

blocks.note: the Mini is a small British car
the last letter of 'is'
to tax someone, as in taxing their patience, is to try them

annotation.surface: A government department is at last blocking a vehicle levy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Car tax' looks like one thing, a road levy, but it is two: the car and a verb meaning strain.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain the big state departments are named ministries, such as the Ministry of Defence, each run by a minister.

entries.clue: Ordinary outlaw completely losing heart (5)

blocks.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
ALL, meaning completely, without its middle L

annotation.surface: An everyday criminal has lost his nerve entirely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun, a bandit, but here it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Banal means dull and ordinary, lacking originality.

entries.clue: Many men put out about female’s conclusion (7)

indicatorNotes.put out: the letters are disturbed into a new order
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of MEN and PUT, rearranged
the last letter of 'female'

annotation.surface: A crowd of men are annoyed about how a woman's story ended.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'put out' as annoyed, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange 'men put', and 'about' then wraps those letters around the woman's last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a great many.

entries.clue: Condemned Parliament’s condescending attitude? (11)

indicatorNotes.Condemned: the letters are doomed, broken up and recast

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, possessive S included

annotation.surface: A critic denounces the patronising stance of Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: Again the possessive S belongs to the fodder. The question mark flags that paternalism is only one form of condescension: a father-knows-best attitude.
annotation.definitionFit: Paternalism is treating people like children for their own supposed good, which is a condescending attitude.

entries.clue: Rehearsals of Brahms and Liszt in Potteries (11)

indicatorNotes.Brahms and Liszt: rhyming slang for 'pissed', meaning drunk, so the letters reel about

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Two composers are having their works practised in the Potteries.
annotation.walkthrough: The composers are not people but an indicator: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, British slang for drunk. The Potteries are the pottery towns around Stoke-on-Trent in Staffordshire.
annotation.definitionFit: Rehearsals are repeated run-throughs, so repetitions.

entries.clue: Start to snooze after endless sweet course (8)

indicatorNotes.endless: the last letter is cut off
indicatorNotes.after: the S comes after the sweet

blocks.note: SYLLABUB, a creamy whipped pudding, without its last B
the first letter of 'snooze'

annotation.surface: Nodding off after a pudding at the end of a long meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet course' reads as the dessert course of a meal; in fact 'course' alone is the definition, a course of study. A syllabub is an old British dessert of whipped cream and wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of what a course of study covers, and can stand for the course itself.

entries.clue: Squawk that hurt chicken (6)

blocks.note: a squawk is a loud cry, a yell
OW is what you say when something hurts

annotation.surface: A hen cries out in pain.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard picture makes 'chicken' a bird, but it is the adjective meaning cowardly.
annotation.definitionFit: Yellow and chicken are both informal words for cowardly.

entries.clue: Book for children by strait-laced queen (6)

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

annotation.surface: A children's book written by a prudish queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' reads as authorship, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary schoolbook for teaching children to read.

entries.clue: Ex-PM reportedly eats in exclusive part of London (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as it is said, so a word is spelt differently from how it sounds

blocks.note: Theresa May, Prime Minister 2016 to 2019
eats, as a noun, is food, which is fare

annotation.surface: A former Prime Minister is said to dine in a smart corner of London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eats' looks like a verb but is the slang noun for food. Mayfair is a wealthy district of the West End.
annotation.definitionFit: Mayfair is one of London's most expensive districts.

entries.clue: List of things to do in Copenhagen daily (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is contained in the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the tail of the city into the start of 'daily'

annotation.surface: A to-do list printed in a Danish daily newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words, which is why the Danish capital is there.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin for 'things to be done', it is the running order of business at a meeting.

entries.clue: Daniel upset Gladys, briefly top-billed actress (7,4)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters are knocked over into a new order
indicatorNotes.briefly: the name is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: used as printed
GLADYS without its last letter

annotation.surface: A man named Daniel has offended a woman named Gladys.
annotation.walkthrough: The two names look like characters in a drama; together, once Gladys is shortened, they are the letters of the star.
annotation.definitionFit: The leading lady is the actress playing the main female role, so she gets top billing.

entries.clue: Incendiary crime of unclothed clergymen (5)

indicatorNotes.unclothed: stripped of its outer layer: first and last letters

blocks.note: PARSONS with its first and last letters removed

annotation.surface: A scandal: naked vicars caught committing a fiery offence.
annotation.walkthrough: The absurd picture of undressed clergy hides the instruction to strip PARSONS of its outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

entries.clue: Flog prisoner here, we hear (4)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is a sound, to be spelt another way

blocks.note: a prisoner is kept in a cell

annotation.surface: A demand to whip a prisoner, as we are told happens here.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flog' means beat in the surface but is British slang for sell.
annotation.definitionFit: To flog something, in British slang, is to sell it.

entries.clue: Top bishop, perhaps one with role at wedding (4,3)

blocks.note: top means the best
a bishop is one of the chessmen; 'perhaps' marks it as an example

annotation.surface: A senior bishop might officiate at a wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: The wedding makes the bishop a clergyman, but he is a chess piece, one example of a man on the board.
annotation.definitionFit: The best man attends the groom and has a set role at the wedding.

entries.clue: Mental picture of one’s later years (5)

blocks.note: one is = I am, so I'M
age as in old age

annotation.surface: Picturing what one's old age will be like.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S is 'is', not a possessive: 'one is' becomes I AM, contracted to I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the sense of image used in 'the image of her face stayed with him'.

entries.clue: November in joyless seaside attraction (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the N goes inside the next word

blocks.note: N is November in the radio alphabet
joyless means sad

annotation.surface: A gloomy November at a seaside resort.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joyless seaside attraction' reads as one grim phrase, but joyless belongs to the wordplay and the definition starts at 'seaside'.
annotation.definitionFit: Sand, as in a sandy beach, is what draws people to the seaside.

entries.clue: Soothing stuff spoken in royal residence (8)

blocks.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
oral means spoken, not written

annotation.surface: An ointment is talked about in a royal house.
annotation.walkthrough: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is the British royal family's Scottish home.
annotation.definitionFit: Balmoral is a castle owned by the monarch, a royal residence.
